title: Paneer bhurji
summary: Crumbled paneer cooked down with onion, tomato and spice. Fifteen minutes, one pan, 25 g of protein without touching an egg.
steps: Heat the oil, crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and cook 4-5 minutes until it turns translucent and just starts to catch colour at the edges.
Ginger and chilli in, 30 seconds, then the powdered spices and salt with a splash of water so they do not burn.
Add the tomatoes (and pepper if using) and cook 4-5 minutes, pressing them down, until they collapse and the oil separates at the edges.
Fold in the crumbled paneer. Two minutes, no more - paneer turns rubbery if you cook it hard.
Off the heat, stir through garam masala, coriander and lemon.
tips: Crumble the paneer with your fingers, not a grater - you want irregular pieces, some big enough to bite.
If your paneer is shop-bought and firm, soak it in warm water for 10 minutes first and it softens right up.
Leftovers go into a wrap the next day and are arguably better.
health_notes: Paneer is roughly 18 g protein per 100 g. This is one of the few vegetarian mains that hits a real protein target without any powder or supplement.

source.adapted: Home-style bhurji, made with a tablespoon of oil rather than the usual ghee-heavy version.
